questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first take your foot off the gas pedal to slow down. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with slow, steady pressure.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Driving slower reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: A driver who goes much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Should not let other cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be unsafe. On two-lane roads with traffic backing up behind you, you must pull over and let other cars pass. Only drive well below the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded areas under trees or buildings. These spots freeze faster than the rest of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: Mixing drugs with alcohol:

options.text: Increases your chance of causing a crash.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Reduces alcohol's effect on your driving.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your chance of causing a crash.
questions.explanation: Drugs (including prescription and over-the-counter medicines) can impair your brain and driving ability. Mixing drugs with alcohol greatly increases your crash risk.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit in school zones?
questions.explanation: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit in school zones is 20 mph. Drive carefully in these areas because children and pedestrians may cross into traffic.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must drive at a speed that is reasonable and safe. Your speed must fit the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. You must also obey all speed limit signs.

questions.question: You are in the right lane and want to move to the left lane on a highway. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure no cars are in the lane. Always signal when you change lanes.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, you must:

options.text: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes. If you are in an intersection, pass through first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. This helps other drivers see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When you drive faster, what happens to your field of vision?

options.text: It makes it easier to see cross traffic.

questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As speed increases, you see less around you. You must stay alert for hazards.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights in Massachusetts?

options.text: During the day in good weather.
When the temperature drops below freezing.

questions.explanation: Massachusetts law requires headlights when driving in tunnels. Headlights help you see better in areas with low visibility.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
Driving in a way that is more dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving for weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians are doing.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children out, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the children wave at you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Watch for children walking along the side of the road after the bus stops. Always drive carefully around children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highway ahead is undergoing maintenance.
questions.explanation: Orange construction signs warn drivers about work zones. This sign alerts you to a construction area ahead. Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: When driving on wet pavement, what should you remember?

options.text: Pavement is especially slippery right after it rains.
Give yourself extra space to stop.

questions.explanation: Wet roads are very slippery, especially right after it rains. Your tires travel on a layer of water and oil. Slow down in heavy rain or when water is on the road to keep traction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you of a steep hill. Adjust your speed to drive safely.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the distance it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change with speed and road conditions. Steering ability does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line between your lane and the passing lane is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic going the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What is distracted driving?

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Paying attention to the road helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which statement is true about wet roads?

options.text: Tires work less well when you drive faster.
Water does not affect good tires.
Deep water is safer than shallow water.
Roads become more slippery when you slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires work less well when you drive faster.
questions.explanation: When you drive faster on a wet road, your tires cannot remove water as well. If you go too fast, your tires will lose grip and you will hydroplane, or slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs or other roadside objects.

questions.question: Why does night driving require more caution?

options.text: More traffic is on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.
Accidents happen more often at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it is darker and drivers cannot see as well. From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people and vehicles are not visible from 500 feet away, you must use your headlights.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you may continue through carefully.
